questions.q: A bullet of& $4g$ mass is fired from a gun of mass $4kg .$~If the bullet moves with the muzzle speed of $50{ms}^{1},$& the impulse imparted to the gun and velocity of recoil of gun are&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By momentum conservation,
$4 \times {10}^{- 3} ( 50 - v ) - 4v = 0$
$v = \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 50}{4 + 4 \times {10}^{- 3}} \approx 0 . 05\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$
Impulse $J = mv = 4 \times . 05 = 0 . 2kgms^{- 1}$

questions.q:
Consider a block kept on an inclined plane (inclined at $45 °$) as shown in the figure. If the force required to just push it up the incline is $2$ times the force required to just prevent it from sliding down, the coefficient of friction between the block and inclined plane $( µ )$ is equal to :

.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The forces acting on block& is shown in above figure.

Here, normal force,& $N = mgcos45 °$~and frictional force,~$f = \muN$.

Balancing the force along incline, we have

${F}_{1} = mgsin45 ° + f = mgsin45 ° + \muN$

$⇒ {F}_{1} = \dfrac{mg}{2} + \mu mgcos45 °$

$⇒ {F}_{1} = \dfrac{mg}{2} \left(1 + \mu\right)$

Now, the forces acting on block to just push it up on inclined plane is shown below.

Balancing the force along incline, we have

${F}_{2} = mgsin45 ° - f = mgsin45 ° - \muN$

=\dfrac{mg}{2} \left(1 - \mu\right)$

Given,~${F}_{1} = 2{F}_{2}$

$⇒ $\dfrac{mg}{2} \left(1 + \mu\right) = 2\dfrac{mg}{2} \left($1 - \mu\right)$

$⇒ 1 + \mu = 2 - 2\mu$

$⇒ \mu = $\dfrac{1}{3} =$0 . 33$

$

questions.q: A particle of mass $\mathrm{m}$ is moving in a straight line with momentum p. Starting at time $t=0,$ a force $F=k$ t acts in the same direction on the moving particle during time interval T so that its momentum changes from $\mathrm{p}$ to $3 \mathrm{p}$. Here $k$ is a constant. The value of $\mathrm{T}$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: From Newton's second law $\frac{\mathrm{dp}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{kt}$ Integrating both sides we get, $\int_{\mathrm{p}}^{3 \mathrm{p}} \mathrm{dp}=\int_{0}^{\mathrm{T}} \mathrm{ktdt} \Rightarrow[\mathrm{p}]_{\mathrm{p}}^{3 \mathrm{p}}=\mathrm{k}\left[\frac{\mathrmt^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{\mathrm{T}}\Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{p}=\frac{\mathrm{kT}^{2}}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{T}=2 \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{k}}}$

$mgsin\theta = \mu mgcos\theta$

$tan\theta = \mu = 0 . 75$

$⇒ \theta = 37$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{R - h}{R}$

$\cos 37 = \dfrac{1 - h}{1} ⇒ h = 0 . 2$

questions.q: A block of mass $M$ slides down on a rough inclined plane with constant velocity. The angle made by the incline plane with horizontal is $\theta$. The magnitude of the contact force will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the block moves with constant velocity, so force on the block should be balanced. The forces acting on the block are its weight, normal contact force and& friction. The contact force is vector sum of normal contact and friction. As the forces are balanced, the contact force should be equal and opposite to its weight.

$∴$Contact force~$= Mg$

questions.solution:
Limiting friction force is, ${f}_\max = \mu \left($mgcos$\theta\right)

$= 2 .5 $\sqrt{3}$N$

For first case:

For second case:

$= 25 - 2 .5 $\sqrt{3}

$∴ {F}_{1} - {F}_{2} = 5$\sqrt{3}$N$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : An electric fan continues to rotate for some time after the current is switched off.

Reason R: Fan continues to rotate due to inertia of motion.

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When a fan is rotating, it acquires some kinetic energy. When the switch is off, because of its motion, it continues rotating for some time until it stops because of the air friction. So it& is due to inertia of motion that fan continues to rotate.&

Hence, both& A& and& R& are correct and& R& is the correct explanation of& A.

questions.q: A monkey of mass $50$ kg climbs on a rope which can withstand the tension  \left(T\right)$~of $350N$. If monkey initially climbs down with an acceleration of $4ms^{- 2}$ and then climbs up with an acceleration of $5ms^{- 2}$. Choose the correct option  \left(g = 10ms^{- 2}\right)$
options: Rope will break while climbing upward
Rope will break while going downward
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let& ${a}_{1}$~be the acceleration of monkey while moving down.

F.B.D of monkey while moving downward

Using Newton's second law of motion,

$mg - T = m{a}_{1}$

$∴ 500 - T = 50 \times 4 ⇒ T = 300N$

Let~${a}_{2}$~be the acceleration of monkey while moving up.

F.B.D of monkey while moving up

Using Newton's second law of motion

$T - mg = m{a}_{2}$

$⇒ T - 500 = 50 \times 5$

$⇒ T = 750N$

Breaking strength of rope~$= 750 - 300 = 350N$

$∴$ Rope will break while monkey is moving upward.

questions.solution:
The forces acting on two masses are shown below.

Here,& $N$~is~normal to the incline and tension~$T$~along the string up the incline.~As the string and the pulley are all light and smooth, the tension in the string is uniform everywhere.

Thus, equating,~${m}_{2}g = {m}_{1}gsinθ$

$\to sinθ = \dfrac{m2}{m1} = \dfrac{3}{5}$~and~$cosθ = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Normal force on ${m}_{1}$~is~$N = {m}_{1}gcosθ = 5gcosθ$

$= 5 × 10 × \dfrac{4}{5} = 40N$

questions.q: A force on an object of mass $100g$ is \left(10\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j}\right)N$. The position of that object at $t = 2s$ is \left(a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j}\right)m$ after starting from rest. The value of $\dfrac{a}{b}$ will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{F}m = \dfrac{10\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j}}{0 . 1} = 100\overset{^}{i} + 50\overset{^}{j}$

Displacement covered in vector form can be written as,~$\overset{→}{s} = \overset{→}{u}t + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{→}{a}t^{2}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{s} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(100\overset{^}{i} + 50\overset{^}{j}\right)\left(2\right)2$

,~$⇒ \overset{→}{s} = 200\overset{^}{i} + 100\overset{^}{j}$

Comparing it with,~$\overset{→}{s} = a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j}$, we get $a = 200\text{ \text{ and } }b = 100$

Therefore,~$\dfrac{a}{b} = 2$

questions.q: Four forces are acting at a point $P$ in equilibrium as shown in figure. The ratio of force ${F}_{1}$ to ${F}_{2}$ is $1: x$ where x =_____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Here,& $\theta = 45 °$

Applying equilibrium conditions,

Taking components along $x$~& $y$

Considering right side positive,~$∑ {F}_{x} = 0$

${F}_{1} + 1\sin 45 ° - 2\sin 45 ° = 0{F}_{1} = 2\sin 45 ° - 1\sin 45 °$

${F}_{1} = \sqrt{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{2 - 1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Taking~upward positive,$∑ {F}_{y} = 0$

$1\cos 45 ° + 2\cos 45 ° - {F}_{2} = 0{F}_{2} = 1\cos 45 ° + 2\cos 45 °$

${F}_{2} = \sqrt{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{2 + 1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

${F}_{1}: {F}_{2} = 1: 3$

$x = 3$
